architecture.mechanism: Weekly thrombolytic locks enzymatically degrade forming fibrin sheaths and thrombi within the catheter lumen, preventing flow-limiting occlusion.
architecture.intervention: Integrate a scheduled weekly thrombolytic lock protocol using an approved agent instilled into each catheter lumen during interdialytic dwell periods, replacing standard heparin or citrate locks for patients with early flow degradation.
architecture.expected_effect: Sustained blood flow patency beyond the first week of insertion by dissolving nascent fibrin sheaths before they mature into complete occlusions, reducing catheter removal rates while maintaining hemodialysis safety protocols.
architecture.falsification_test: Conduct a randomized controlled trial comparing weekly thrombolytic locks to standard anticoagulant locks in newly inserted tunneled hemodialysis catheters, measuring mean blood flow rate at 4 weeks; if the thrombolytic group shows no statistically significant improvement in flow rate or reduction in dysfunction events, the mechanism is falsified.
